To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have derived and numerically validated some asymptotic expressions for the convergence rate of classical and quasi-optimal SWR methods applied to the linear and nonlinear one dimensional Schrödigner equations.

we derive and numerically verify some asymptotic convergence estimates of Classical and quasi-optimal Schwarz waveform relaxation methods applied to the stationary states computation of the one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations.

the convergence rates of the classical and quasi-optimal SWR methods applied to the imaginary-time linear and nonlinear Schrodinger equations are asymptotically equal to the square root of the number of subdomains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and design of efficient and robust algorithms for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in quantum physics.
the development of new numerical methods for solving the stationary Gross-Pitaevski equation.
a convergence analysis of a SWR domain decomposition method for solving a linear Schrödingerequation with space dependent potential and a Gross-Pitaevski equation with a space dependent potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the convergence rate of a quasi-optimal SWR method applied to the computation by the NGF method of the stationary states for a one-dimensional Schrôdinger equation with a space-dependent nonlinearity is of the order of the number of subdomains.
the convergence rates of SWR methods applied to the imaginary-time formulation are determined by the eigenvalues of the operator involved in the NGF equation and the discretization scheme.
the convergence rates for the linear and nonlinear Schrodinger equations are the same, and are given by the same expressions as in the advection reaction diffusion case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the convergence of the SWR method is governed by the spectral properties of the inhomogeneous pseudolaplacian and that the spectral gap is a good indicator of convergence.

we have obtained a general theory of convergence of the SWR methods applied to the NGF formulation of the linear and nonlinear Schrodinger equation, and we have derived explicit expressions of the convergence rate for both the classical and quasi-optimal SWR algorithms.
we have developed a general framework for the convergence analysis of the SWR domain decomposition methods for linear and nonlinear PDEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convergence rate of the SWR method is independent of the discretization step size.
the convergence rate of SWR methods is determined by the spectral properties of the underlying operator and the way the subdomains are defined.
SWR methods are very robust and can be used for the stationary states of a large class of nonlinear Schröinger equations.
